theses.subject: Oil & Gas Producers
theses.thesis: The dominant eligible trend with the strongest durability bar (0.71) and deep breadth (0.929) among scorable names. Absolute-trend gate is validated for drawdown control in this market, and Oil & Gas clears it. Crowding (z 1.19) is a size-down caution, not a fade — per guardrails, cap rather than fight the leader.
evidence: crowding_z 1.19, crowded true — reflexivity argues against fading
theses.dissent: Crowded one-narrative energy is exactly where attention spikes mark tops; the same breadth and crowding that support the trend also signal late-cycle concentration, and a mean-revert blowoff in WTI would hit XEG.TO hardest given its leadership.

falsifier.text: XEG.TO closes below its own 50-day moving average while the S&P/TSX benchmark remains positive over the same window

theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Second-strongest eligible scorable trend (score 0.635, durability 0.63, trend hurst, breadth 0.429). Not crowded (z 0.15). Offers a non-energy alternative with trend-gate clearance, though breadth is thinner than Oil & Gas and it ranks far behind the leader.
theses.dissent: Canadian banks are rate-sensitive and concentrated; their trend is weaker than the energy leader and may simply be a defensive residual bid that fades when the one-narrative energy focus rotates away.

falsifier.text: ZEB.TO underperforms XEG.TO by more than 5% over the next 20 trading days

theses.subject: Technology
theses.thesis: Eligible but crowded (z 1.36, highest crowding in the ranks) with a barely negative score (-0.037) and mixed hurst. Crowding here is a size-down caution only, but with no positive momentum leg to justify staying, the cleanest expression is to stand aside rather than commit to this crowded, directionless theme.
theses.dissent: High breadth (0.80) with heavy crowding could reflect genuine institutional accumulation that precedes a trend leg; avoiding it risks missing the rotation if energy leadership fades into tech.

falsifier.text: XIT.TO beats XEG.TO by more than 8% over the next 20 trading days
